claim: A CAS ref-prefix enumeration can omit durable ref-log objects: Probe A observed two holes at 16:47:38 that were missing from the pre-fold scan while HEAD verified both objects as present.

In the observed list-incompleteness occurrence, ref-log objects `0x1430c`, `0x1430d`, and `0x1430e` were uploaded in strict ID order at 16:47:19.211480, 16:47:19.212340, and 16:47:19.213680 respectively.
The first walk returned ref-log object `0x1430e` after its upload, but did not return the two earlier objects `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` even though they had been durable for 1.3–2.2 ms at that point.
A measurement of 65,263 ref-log uploads found zero out-of-order uploads after partitioning by writer epoch.
For the observed disagreement, `ch2` deleted zero ref objects over all time, `ch1` deleted zero ref objects during 16:47:00–16:48:00, and `ch2` deleted zero ref objects during that interval.

`blob_storage_log` records object writes and deletes but not LIST calls, so the observed evidence bounds timing without identifying whether the listing failure was a dropped page, a boundary error, or another store behavior.
GC must not trust LIST completeness, independently of whether the object store is RustFS or AWS S3.
The three observed ref-log keys were deleted at 16:53:59 after folding aborted and a later complete enumeration reclaimed them; this occurrence produced no leak.
Every persisted CAS object is a text file with header `{"type":"cas_<object>","v":N}`, a body consisting of JSON, sorted NDJSON, or a raw payload zone, and an optional `{"n":…}` trailer.

Can-grow-large CAS object types use a `.zst` key suffix and exactly one zstd frame with checksum enabled and declared content size checked against the allocation cap; always-small and deterministic types are raw.
`CasTextFormat.{h,cpp}` is the only code that knows the persisted CAS text-file shape.

The CAS object inventory has no binary formats and no protobuf dependency; `cas_run` is sorted NDJSON read as a non-seekable stream with a whole-file seal checksum, while the part manifest is the single `PayloadHybrid` object with a text header, descriptor metadata, sorted entry records, `{"n":…}` trailer, and banner-framed raw inline-payload zone.

The ref transaction log is stored under `cas/ns/stream/<life_id>/_log/…​.zst`, complete ref snapshots under `cas/ns/stream/<life_id>/_snap/…​.zst`, and mutable life checkpoints under `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_ckpt`.

Part manifests are stored under `cas/manifests/<ns>/<epoch-hex>-<seq-hex>/<ordinal>.zst`, blob envelopes use `CasLayout::blobKey`, blob freshness sidecars use `CasLayout::blobMetaKey`, and GC source-edge runs use `gc/gen/<g>/…​/runs`.
The only persisted format version field is the header `v`; readers reject `v > G_BUILD` with `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION` before reading the body.

An additive format change introduces a tolerant key without bumping `v`, while a breaking change bumps `v`, records `changePoints`, writes down to the pool floor, and relies on the raised floor to fence old builds out.

Deterministic formats such as `cas_fold_seal` and `cas_run` use strict keys and pinned raw encoding; a `putDeterministicArtifact` conflict is resolved by re-encoding at the version of the existing object.
A persisted key prefixed with `!` is critical, and a reader that does not understand it fails closed.

`openObject` rejects a compressed body under a raw-compression policy, but passes a non-zstd body through verbatim under an `Always` policy as an intentional uncompressed-repair path; in normal operation `Always` objects are read through `.zst`-suffixed keys.
A CAS blob is immutable, shared, and keyed by a content digest; identity is established by re-hashing bytes, with no trust-the-checksum shortcut, and its freshness sidecar is `blobKey` plus `.meta`.

A CAS manifest is an immutable full file tree whose entries reference blobs or inline bytes; small per-part files such as `uuid.txt` and `checksums.txt` are inline tree entries rather than separate objects.

A ref table is one mutable naming layer per table namespace `SERVER_ID/TABLE_UUID`, implemented as an append-only transaction log plus periodic snapshots and mutable checkpoints under one namespace LIFE.
All ref-table mutations use a precommit/promote two-step so a manifest has an owner before it becomes visible.

A server root is a single-writer mount slot identified by `server_root_id`, with lease and writer-epoch fencing stored at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/{owner,epoch,mount}`; a fenced writer cannot mutate the pool using stale state.
CAS GC computes blob in-degrees from manifest-to-blob source edges, condemns zero-in-degree blobs, and later deletes them with exact-token conditional deletes so a concurrent re-upload wins.
The CAS write path hashes payloads, uploads or adopts blobs after a HEAD proves presence, stages a manifest, calls `precommitAdd`, and promotes the ref to committed in the ref log.
The CAS read path parses a disk path with `Parts/PartPathParser`, resolves the ref table to a manifest, and reads either stored blob objects or inline manifest bytes.
`ContentAddressedExchange` replication transfers manifest bytes and lets the receiver adopt listed blobs by hash without payload transfer; decode or promote failure falls back to ordinary byte fetch.

A GC round takes or renews the leader lease, collects source edges, folds per-shard in-degrees, condemns new zero-in-degree blobs, exact-token-deletes previously condemned blobs whose state is unchanged, and seals the round with one CAS on `gc/state`.
The CAS source tree follows `Primitives → Formats → Backend → Pool → Gc → Tools ≈ Parts → facade`; `Tools` and `Parts` are siblings with no include edge between them.

The include-direction rule permits a file to include only its own layer and layers to its left; the staging sweeper and `probeConditionalCopy` are named exceptions that reach directly into `IObjectStorage`.
A CAS disk is an `object_storage` disk with `metadata_type` set to `cas`; `<readonly>1</readonly>` disables mount-slot claims, capability probes, and writes.
The read-only `clickhouse-disks` CAS tools include `fsck`, `cas-inspect`, `cas-gc-dryrun`, `cas-gc-rebuild`, and `cas-drop-member`.
`system.cas_log` emits one row per CAS protocol event and is the primary audit trail for investigating pool state.
All CAS unit-test suite names start with `Cas`, so `--gtest_filter='Cas*'` runs the complete CAS suite; the suite generator fails loudly when a suite does not match.

The CAS soak harness derives a deterministic operation ledger from one `--seed` integer using a `splitmix64` stream, and checkpoints compare exact integer aggregates on both replicas and against an in-process oracle before running `clickhouse-disks cas-fsck`.

The soak harness defaults inserts to synchronous mode (`async_insert=0`); B138 found sync `ABORTED` retries idempotent, while B139 found async retries can lose rows through the dedup-token-vs-part hazard.

Each adversarial scenario should run independently against a fresh pool prefix `<scenario>/<seed>/<run_id>` and should end at a quiesced checkpoint with synchronized replicas, empty replication and mutation queues, no active merges, and forced GC rounds to a declared fixpoint.

Scenario reports must include `report.md`, `report.json`, `metrics.sqlite`, raw system-table extracts, pool-size samples, and container-resource samples, and missing observability data must fail loudly rather than being silently converted to `pass`.

Every positive scenario requires replica-oracle SQL agreement, `clickhouse-disks cas-fsck --detail` with `dangling = 0`, and `clickhouse-disks cas-gc-dryrun` candidates contained in the quiescent `cas-fsck` unreachable set.

A scenario must reject `system.cas_log` rows with `read_missing`, `dangling_access`, `corrupt_dangle`, `corrupt_decode`, `snap_journal_incoherent`, or `exception` outcomes unless it is an explicitly negative fail-closed test.
After forced GC, `unreachable` must be zero unless a scenario deliberately abandons writes; any residual must be classified by object class and proven bounded and expected.
For CPU, off-CPU, and memory investigations, scenario reports must rank `system.trace_log` stacks separately for `CPU`, `Real`, and `Memory` trace types.

The scenario suite treats `CASBlobPut`, `CASBlobPutDeduplicated`, `CASBlobHead`, `CASBlobHeadMiss`, `CASBlobHeadFirst`, `CASBlobBodyPutAvoided`, `CASBlobDeduplicationCacheHit`, `CASBlobDelete`, `CASBlobList`, `CASRootGet`, `CASRootHead`, `CASRootCompareSwap`, `CASRootCompareSwapConflict`, `CASRootList`, `CASGCGet`, `CASGCHead`, `CASGCCompareSwap`, `CASGCDelete`, and `CASGCList` as core CAS operation counters.

During precommit-first publishing, a durable precommit may name a manifest while blob upload is still in progress, so mid-write `fsck` and dry-run results are not hard correctness verdicts; structural assertions belong at quiescent checkpoints.
S01 requires large-blob process memory to stay bounded by buffers and overhead rather than blob size, scratch usage to return near baseline after commit, and large blobs to use multipart operations.
S02 requires a repeated large content blob to avoid remote body upload, with second-insert pool growth limited to manifests, refs, sidecars, and unique small metadata.

S03 requires idle GC duration to scale with changed owner transitions rather than total live blobs, with `CASBlobList` equal to zero in regular journal-driven rounds unless an orphan sweep or `fsck` intentionally lists blobs.
S05 requires idle tables not to dominate GC CPU or S3 GET counts; ref body reads must be driven by new logs since per-table cursors rather than table count, and cursor regression must be reported.
S06 requires a 10000-column manifest either to commit below the hard cap or to fail early with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, and a subset-column read must not fetch every large blob body.
S07 requires a manifest-limit failure to return `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, publish no live ref to the rejected manifest, and leave only bounded reclaimable staged debris.

S08 requires CAS ref writes to stay on the per-table single-writer append lane, with ref-object count within `n_parts * 4 + 16` and no CA metadata exception beyond expected MergeTree part-count pressure.

S12 requires at most one GC leader to make progress per round, duplicate leaders to cause no wrong deletes, and shared physical blob bytes to remain near unique content bytes rather than `replica_count * content_bytes`.
S13 requires that a stale GC leader cannot delete after losing the lease or fence race and that abandoned precommits do not grow without bound.
S16 requires resurrection to use writer-owned source bytes rather than a condemned object, and requires `blob_reuse_resurrect` to fire at least once during the hot-content cycle.
S17 requires detached parts to remain reachable until explicitly dropped, after which dropped detached content becomes reclaimable by GC.
S18 requires a frozen shadow namespace to keep blobs alive independently of live table refs until `SYSTEM UNFREEZE` releases the shadow refs.
S20 requires follower replicas to publish their own refs and sidecars without reuploading existing large blobs, so pool growth is metadata-only per replica.
S22 requires bounded object-store `503`, `429`, slow-response, and connection-close faults to increase visible latency without data loss, unbounded retries, or committed partial refs.
The known-present blob cache is a bounded cost hint: reducing `deduplication_cache_bytes` may lower `CASBlobDeduplicationCacheHit` but must not change correctness.
S27 requires duplicate or unstable root-shard LIST pages to force safe rereads and treat ambiguous keys as changed, preserving correctness while exposing extra `CASRootGet` cost.

The allocation-fault scenario S42 treats a post-durable-install allocation failure as allowed to fail queries but not invariants: after quiescence and restart, `fsck` must report `dangling=0`, `unaccounted=0`, and `stale_edge=0`, with every acknowledged insert present.

The 2026-07-15 reboot checkpoint recorded the all-tree part-files plan as closed at 12/12 with approved reviews and a green milestone soak, codecs-v3 phases 2/4/5/7 committed, drafts for phases 2/4/7 parked in worktrees, and stateless gate #49 killed two minutes after dispatch.
The sanctioned full CA-default stateless lane is `python -m ci.praktika run "Stateless tests (arm_binary, content_addressed storage, parallel)"`.

After the full CA-default lane, failures are triaged as real CA bugs, genuinely unsupported tests needing a reasoned `no-content-addressed-storage` tag, environment/configuration-sensitive cases, or flakes/timeouts; no fixes are made mid-run.

Codecs-v3 draft integration requires reading `DRAFT.md`, applying `DRAFT.patch` with `git apply --3way`, building and running named tests, committing using the draft split, reviewing the pinned diff, and then running phase exit criteria plus a milestone soak.
Codecs-v3 integration order requires phase 2 before phase 4, permits phase 7 before or after phases 2 and 4, parks phase 3 until phase 2 is integrated and soaked, and reserves phase 8 for last.

The unattended campaign watchdog is intended to run every 20 minutes and check fresh progress artifacts, disk usage, CPU starvation, Docker debris, and heavy-build versus soak overlap before intervening.

The post-codecs campaign queue lists `#36` S36 MOVE PART/PARTITION scenarios, `#37` merge upload-retry investigation, `#38` production-scale scenarios 01–36, and `#40` CAS unit-test ASan compatibility including TSan verification of the rev.6 F3-1a race.
The roadmap is a DONE/history roll-up; `BACKLOG.md` is the canonical list of still-pending CAS work, and the former root-shard-axis items are obsolete under the per-table snapshot+log model.
The Merkle `treeId` tree layer was rejected because it added complexity without a correctness benefit; tree objects are manifest-internal.
The EBR GC core was rejected because per-object epoch state did not scale; GC uses incarnation-token identity instead.
Integer in-degree refcounting was rejected because non-atomic folding under concurrent leaders could undercount; the source-edge set replaced it.
The `_registry` namespace registry was removed because repeated create/drop operations caused monotone growth; per-shard incarnation enables namespace-level reclaim instead.
CAS manifests use `cas/manifests/` as the immutable hot/cold split from mutable ref shards, and the pool layout includes `blobs/`, `cas/refs/`, `cas/manifests/`, `roots/`, and `gc/`.
`manifest_soft_limit` paces CAS writes and `manifest_hard_limit` throws `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` before any ref is published.
The `manifest_hash` field on the Keeper `/parts` znode was rejected because replication remains disk-agnostic; the manifest ID travels in-band during fetch and manifest divergence is benign.

A 10,000-row by 10 KB `FixedString` INSERT measured peak CA memory at 144.5 MiB versus 135.5 MiB locally; the approximately 9 MiB delta came from `ContentAddressedTransaction::writeFile` staging and hash buffering, and test `03829` was raised from 150M to 170M.

A deposed leader's pre-CAS `clearSparedMeta` could leave stray `Clean` metadata over a `delete_pending` blob, allowing a writer to reuse the condemned exact token and a pending exact-token redelete to delete the live reuse; add-only GC freshness metadata fixed this INV_NO_LOSS risk.
Two-phase graduation uses `delete_pending`: pre-CAS deletes apply only to previously published pending entries, and deletion lags condemnation by one pass.
Every per-round GC artifact is keyed by `(gen, attempt = lease.seq)`, so artifacts from a deposed leader remain under an unadopted attempt.

The retired-in-snapshot design stores condemnation state as `kCondemned` sentinel rows in the source-edge run and stores per-shard `condemned_summary` in the fold seal; the merge therefore uses two cursors instead of three.
The separate `RetiredSet` object family, `retiredKey`, `GcState::retired_refs`, `FormatId::RetiredSet`, and magic `CART` were deleted and the `CART` value is reserved never to be reused.
An empty-delta and empty-retired GC shard is pure ref-carry and performs zero run-object I/O; `RunRef` carries `shard` and `generation` and consumers resolve runs through seal refs.

Streaming GC run reads use true ranged reads and `getStream`; opening a run costs three requests (`head`, tail `get`, and body `getStream`), or four when a large footer is present, and each `seek` costs one ranged GET per block.
B207 was fixed by re-resolving referencing refs in `runFsck` when the initial HEAD is absent; only a current ref over an absent object is classified as dangling.
GC discovery no longer performs the roots-tree quadratic: it lists flat `cas/refs/` and uses streamed pagination with `start_after=cursor`.

Phase 4 Lever A lets a GC round re-adopt the sealed in-degree generation as DEFER when cheap pre-fold signals show no destructive decision; due graduation forces a fold, and the safety gate is `CaGcRoundDeferCore`.
Incremental point-updatable in-degree remains open as Phase 4 Lever B; it is intended to make a non-idle small-delta GC round O(delta).
When any shard is clamped, GC performs no graduation and no pending deletes; a clamp-free pass resumes deletes and emits a `gc_fold_clamp` event.

Ack-floor observability includes `CasGcRetired{Condemned,Spared,Graduated,Redeleted}`, `CasGcHeartbeatFenceOuts`, `CasGcFloorHeldByStaleAck`, a `gc_fence_out` audit event, and `RoundReport` fields for condemned, graduated, redeleted, fence-outs, and `min_ack`.

The CAS read path resolves refs through root-shard decode with TTL and single-flight caches, caches manifests by `(ManifestId, Token)`, performs one ranged S3 GET per column file per part open, and requests only files selected by `lookupPath`.

On the CA-S3 lane, a warm cacheless read measured approximately 141 ms versus 47 ms locally and 186 S3 GETs; an opt-in file-cache disk made warm reads approximately local with zero S3 GETs but made the first cold read about twice as slow.
The CA event log is on by default since `cbe0ffb7608`, and `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log` records per-round GC audit data.
For CA disks, `supportZeroCopyReplication()==false` while `supportsHardLinks()==true`; unsupported operations are rejected by independent gates, while mutations use whole-part transactions.

The first production release still requires Azure real-S3 GC validation, a 4-hour-or-longer chaos soak on a compacting store, and the `B207` fsck race fix as release gates; AWS and GCS validation are recorded as done.

The live AWS GC validation measured 73.8 MB before merge churn, 37.3 MB after merge churn, and 13.9 KB after `DROP TABLE`, with `dedup_ratio=2`, zero anomalies or false 404s across more than 28 rounds, and 30–40 second round duration.

The live GCS validation reclaimed 11 condemned objects through graduation and deletion, recorded a 51-object 20.8 KB metadata pool after DROP-to-zero, and achieved `dedup_ratio=2` with clean fsck results.

The remaining production-release operability gates include `B197` SYSTEM control commands, `B13` migration and mixed-version rollout rules, `B180` pool-format version breadcrumb, `B192` event-name review, `B198` backup/restore runbook, `B48`/`B167a/f` clean shutdown, `B196` S3 permit capping, and `B131` repository hygiene.

The testing roadmap leaves 4-hour continuous chaos, S12 10-replica shared-pool testing, S22 throttling/retry testing, S27 LIST-pagination ambiguity testing, D3 full-round `gc_shards > 1` tests, and B5 per-server-tree integration reconciliation as open work.

Run-file streaming is complete: `RunFileReader` uses ranged reads through `CasObjectStorageBackend::get` and `getStream`, and the whole-run `full` member was removed; delta-runs and compaction remain desirable follow-up work.

The one-shot `manifest_deletes` pipeline consumes owner-removal edges in the same CAS that creates `folded.mf_cleanup` before deletion, so a cap-declined entry is not re-derived and an orphan-manifest sweep of about 100 objects per round cannot keep pace.

The C2 soak comparison recorded 112,518 skipped entries and 110,218 permanently unreachable objects with a cleanup cap of 5000, while disabling the cap drained 223,714 objects with zero unreachable objects.
The setting `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` was removed entirely because bounding the one-shot manifest cleanup phase converts a bounded burst into a permanent leak.

After removal of `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget`, the `manifest_deletes` phase drains all of `folded.mf_cleanup` unconditionally; the `skipped_budget` metric was dropped because it became structurally zero, while `attempted`, `deleted`, and `suppressed` remain.
The replacement test `ManifestCleanupDrainsEntireRoundWithNoSkips` asserts that a five-manifest owner removal deletes all five manifest bodies in the same GC round.

With the cleanup budget temporarily forced from 5000 to 2, `ManifestCleanupDrainsEntireRoundWithNoSkips` reproduced the leak class by deleting 2 of 5 manifest bodies and leaving 3 survivors; the test passed after the cap was removed.

The C2 removal passed the Release CAS gtest run with 2004 tests and zero failures, Release per-suite gate with `pass=278 fail=0 abort=0`, ASan CAS gtest run with 2009 tests and zero failures, and ASan per-suite gate with `pass=296 fail=0 abort=0`.

A durable-retry redesign for real manifest-cleanup bounding, which would move edge consumption past deletion, was intentionally not attempted and is tracked as `[gc-mf-cleanup-durable-retry]` alongside `gc-frontier-one-list`.
The append-ordering measurement contained 65,157 uploads in epoch 1 and 106 uploads in epoch 2, with `out_of_order=0` in both epochs.

The blob-storage audit contains Upload rows for ref-log keys ending `000000000001430c.zst`, `000000000001430d.zst`, and `000000000001430e.zst` at 16:47:19.211480, 16:47:19.212340, and 16:47:19.213680, followed by Delete rows for all three at 16:53:59.552282, 16:53:59.552902, and 16:53:59.553479.
